title: Publish successor v0.5.49 after remediation closure
outOfScope: Changing release workflow security controls, provider configuration, branch protection, signing infrastructure, or supply-chain generators.
Creating, deleting, moving, or reusing any existing immutable tag or provider Release, including v0.5.48.
Creating provider release state except the user-authorized new v0.5.49 tag, Draft Release, assets, and publication through .github/workflows/release.yml after the candidate PR has merged.
Claiming publication or public installation before provider-bound post-publication evidence verifies it.

reasons: Public immutable release publication is a high-risk external operation requiring strict governance.

acceptance: v0.5.48 is classified as unavailable for reuse, and next-release.json plus release-state.json name exactly v0.5.49 as the sole unpublished candidate based on the published v0.5.42 projection.

Candidate metadata, regenerated evidence, and candidate release freeze are created on the dedicated branch; after the green Outcome is archived, premerge freeze and strict release preflight/readiness pass before the candidate PR is created.

After the candidate PR merges and its Work Item evidence is archived, a fresh release.yml rehearsal succeeds for the freshly resolved origin/main SHA and v0.5.49; publication receives only that same-SHA rehearsal receipt.

The controlled provider workflow alone creates v0.5.49 and provider assets, and provider-bound post-publication evidence verifies tag target, Release state, asset names and digests, SBOM, provenance, CI evidence, and tagged quick installation.
The documentation fact gate distinguishes governed historical provider evidence from a current installer-release claim, with a regression test that retains rejection of the latter.

The Contract, Summary, red-or-green Outcome, PR, hosted checks, merge, ai-close-work-item, branch cleanup, and main synchronization truthfully record completion or an exact fail-closed recovery condition.
guidelines: Preserve the distinction between candidate metadata, immutable tags, provider Releases, and public distribution evidence.
Use only repository release commands and the controlled provider workflow to create provider release state or evidence.
Do not retry a failed provider path until its exact failing gate is diagnosed and recorded.
Do not report publication or public installation success before provider-bound post-publication evidence verifies it.

intent.problem: The final audit is closed, but v0.5.48 is an unpublished candidate and cannot be reused. The remaining plan requires a new v0.5.49 candidate, then an immutable provider release bound to the current merged default branch and provider-generated evidence.
constraints: Advance the candidate exactly once from v0.5.48 to v0.5.49; v0.5.48 and all historic tags remain immutable and unavailable for retry.
Use a dedicated candidate PR from origin/main, archive its governance evidence, and merge it before any provider workflow dispatch.
Resolve origin/main immediately before rehearsal; publication must use a successful same-SHA rehearsal receipt and the controlled release.yml workflow.
Do not modify release workflow security, provider configuration, tags, Releases, or assets outside the exact v0.5.49 provider workflow path.
Do not bypass gates or claim success from chat, a candidate file, or stale evidence.
intent.rationale: Separating candidate preparation from source-bound provider promotion prevents version reuse and makes the irreversible public release independently verifiable.

rollbackNote: Before provider publication, revert the candidate PR to retain v0.5.48 as unavailable. After provider mutation, never move or delete the immutable tag; quarantine a failed Draft Release, record the exact failure, and publish only a later corrective patch through a new governed Work Item.
